items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: I'd heard of Coleman Hawkins then... I idolized him as a saxophone player.

ctx.x: I recorded a lot with Cozy when he was recording. And I used to write the arrangements, and I'd be up there rehearsing the band and everything... And one day, I finally played a solo. I hadn't played... Milt, I had such great musicians... What the heck was I doing playing solos when I'd have Coleman Hawkins and Ben Webster... Those guys could play better solos than I, and I knew it! So I wrote the arrangements to feature my men.

So one day I think I had arrangements for I think it was Cozy, and I played a solo. And the guys in the control room came out and said, 'it's about time.' Because see, they had never heard me play a solo. I was just making arrangements. And then finally, one day, I made a solo, and
